channel.title: Original tutorial demo — not live news
channel.description: Fictional local content for learning RSS River.

item.title: A small app can be a place you want to visit
item.description: This is original tutorial demo content, not a published news report. Try starring this paper, switching to the 3D river and flicking it onto the desk.

item.title: AI reading list: keep the source next to the summary
item.description: Demo: a good reading tool preserves the original link. The app stores plain text and lets you open the publisher when you want the complete article.

item.title: Why seconds and milliseconds deserve different names
item.description: Demo coding note: engines often give delta time in seconds while a physics API expects milliseconds. Write the conversion at the boundary.

item.title: Offline-first means your notes survive a train ride
item.description: Demo: refresh news when connected, then read the cached titles and summaries offline. Back up the library before clearing browser storage.

item.title: Make important things a little bigger
item.description: Demo design idea: starred papers are physically larger and float higher. One data flag changes both the reading list and spatial view.

item.title: Read a feed without trusting its markup
item.description: Demo security lesson: convert feed descriptions to text. Never execute a publisher's script or insert its HTML into your app's controls.

item.title: Slow motion is a feature of a calm interface
item.description: Demo: the river is a gentle browse mode. Use the ordinary list and keyboard for precise reading, and keep motion optional.

item.title: Ship the smallest complete version
item.description: Demo: include import, backup, empty states and connection errors before adding an account system. A complete local app is already useful.
